C041.statement: Theorem bodies are checked against a judge-authored proposition and axiom closure restricted to propext/Quot.sound. This is conditional Lean validity. Refusals never count as proofs. The two routes share the same compiler/axiom parser; no independent lean4checker replay is implemented.
limitations: Native bounded controls used installed Lean 4.35.0; no version installation or heavy build.
Neither raw regex scanning nor a subprocess timeout is a parsed command whitelist or an OS sandbox.
Full Lean proofs for every retained case are not claimed; source and data dispositions remain distinct.
Live experiment module is exploratory, with no logit/attention mechanisms or new provider evidence.

C042.statement: Direct finite problem certificates for SAT and normalized-hash-bound RUP/RAT refutations for UNSAT, conditional on canonical-CNF correspondence. Independent truth tables agree on all 512 formula clause sets over 2 variables; 3828 accepted RAT additions preserve satisfiability. There is one checker per kind, not two independent proof replays.
limitations: No CaDiCaL/drat-trim/LRAT execution or formal checker theorem.
Only 512 small formulas exhaustively checked; retained data owner agreement is distinct.
Canonical-CNF equivalence and wellformed family input are necessary admissions.
OOS witness fields are not validated and exploratory routing counts an accepted refusal as VERIFIED/nontrivial.

C043.statement: On well-formed domains with consistent fixed constraints, explicit complete finite coloring checks establish absence of forbidden monochromatic cliques/APs for the submitted string and constraints. Independent finite enumerations cross-check both positive validators and Paley/GG lower witnesses. Negative proofs share C042 DRAT; exact published upper bounds are not derived here.
limitations: Algebraic witness validity does not establish exact Ramsey/VDW upper bounds.
Shared negative encoders/DRAT engine and fixed parsers limit independence.
No Rust/LRAT/native SAT backend or paid model run.
Random search seeded 0 only for reproducible audit replay; timeout is not mathematical infeasibility.

C044.statement: A complete bijective homomorphism between normalized finite multiplication tables certifies isomorphism, and unequal recomputed isomorphism invariants certify nonisomorphism. All 64 retained tables independently satisfy closure, identity, inverse and associativity; order, center and element-order histograms were independently computed. This does not authenticate catalog names or standard numeric IDs.
limitations: No GAP numeric-ID authentication or native independent checker was run.
No claim of full coverage of groups of order<=64.
No source, catalog or historical artifact was changed.

C045.statement: State-sum Kauffman bracket and Fox-matrix Alexander determinant are independently recomputed in Python; 480 finite scalar Leibniz/Bareiss comparisons agree. Polynomial equality and catalog signature matches must be distinguished from knot recognition, and first-checker acceptance alone is weak.
limitations: No general knot-classification or Reidemeister-invariance proof.
No external SnapPy/Sage/Rust checker or paid model run.
Bareiss finite tests do not certify all polynomial inputs.

C046.statement: Completed LPO-decreasing systems with all critical pairs joinable are confluent; joining input equations and deriving submitted rules establishes equivalence to input theory. Current COMPLETE rechecks both directions with two additional bounded completion engines. All 64 acyclic ground rewrite graphs on 4 constants agree with independently computed reachability/confluence; a 2-element countermodel supports rejection of an unsound stronger completion.
limitations: Finite ground controls do not prove arbitrary first-order completion correct.
No kbmag/Rust replay or paid model run.
Budget exhaustion is not a theorem of nontermination.

C047.statement: A nonzero maximal-ansatz determinant excludes fitting recurrences for the stated bounded start range. Positive residual replay proves only agreement at tested indices unless a symbolic source-law argument is supplied; neither checker implements the promised characteristic divisibility or hypergeometric ratio check. 100 independent determinant and 1248 integer-root comparisons pass.
limitations: Finite heldout checks are not all-n mathematical proof.
No Rust or provider execution.
No complete guesser/minimality proof; retained fixture truth not inherited from names.

C048.statement: A nonzero integer point is checked by exact quadratic evaluation. For a nondegenerate diagonal form, a Hilbert symbol of -1 at a genuine prime place supplies a local obstruction. All 108 small primitive modular conic controls agree with both implementations. Official PARI documentation supports the rational-point/local-obstruction output convention; PARI was not run.
limitations: No PARI/Rust execution or broad factorization performance result.
Finite modular probes do not prove the local/global theorem.
Primary probable-prime testing above 64 bits is not deterministic primality certification.

C049.statement: Finite category universal constructions require typed compositions, valid diagrams, and unique factorization for every cone; adjunction further requires actual functors, natural unit/counit and both triangle identities. Conditional finite enumeration is substantial, but certificate binding and input validation fail. A concrete 15-arrow subcategory of finite sets supplies a repeated-object product missed by the implementation.
limitations: Finite poset agreement does not validate arbitrary finite categories or adjunction certificates.
Generators were read but not run because they write original packet paths.
No general categorical theorem or independent formal proof is inferred.

A bounded independent check of 648 unary-model certificates agrees with primary on well-formed domains, disagrees with secondary on 64, and verifies 47 emitted short proofs.
limitations: Two-element finite controls and short unary proofs do not prove completeness or soundness outside their checked domain.
